outcome: No proof of the abundance conjecture for projective klt varieties has been posted since 26 January 2024; the window holds restricted and conditional results (klt with Miyaoka equality, April 2024; conditional equivalence for chi nonzero, June 2024; unconditional smooth dimension at most 5 and klt dimension at most 4 with chi nonzero, May 2025), analytic and Kahler or slc analogues (2025-2026), and a dimension-2 log surface theorem (September 2026), while the general conjecture is still described as open in dimension at least 4.
problem_asks: The bullet, read from its statement alone: (a) for every dimension n (one universal claim, no dimension bound is stated); (b) for every projective variety X with Kawamata log terminal singularities; the bullet names no field or characteristic, and the live Wikipedia article says over a field k; (c) hypothesis: the canonical bundle K_X is nef; (d) conclusion: K_X is semiample, i.e. some positive multiple mK_X is base-point free, equivalently the canonical ring defines a good model / Iitaka fibration. The bullet concerns the variety alone, with no boundary divisor. The literature usually states the conjecture for klt pairs (X, Delta) with K_X + Delta nef, of which the bullet is the Delta = 0 case. The bullet does not ask for the smooth case separately, but smooth varieties are klt, so the smooth case lies inside the bullet.

events.what_happened: Masataka Iwai, Shin-ichi Matsumura and Niklas Muller post arXiv:2404.07568 (v1, 11 Apr 2024). They prove a structure theorem for minimal projective klt varieties X satisfying Miyaoka's equality 3c_2(X) = c_1(X)^2: K_X is semiample, the Kodaira dimension kappa(K_X) is 0, 1 or 2, a maximal quasi-etale cover is smooth, and the Iitaka fibration is described explicitly. The full v4 text (Theorem 1.2) also treats projective klt varieties with nef K_X, giving Miyaoka's inequality (part A) and, under equality, semiampleness (part B). The v4 text states that abundance for minimal klt varieties (its Conjecture 1.1) remains largely unsolved in higher dimensions.
events.revisions: v1 11 Apr 2024 (3 pages per comment field); v2 2 May 2024 (minor); v3 22 Nov 2024 (title changed, main result improved); v4 22 Oct 2025 (Section 5 removed, 4.2 and 6 revised, 'to appear in Proc. London Math. Soc.'). The current title is 'Minimal projective varieties satisfying Miyaoka's equality'; the v1 title ('Abundance theorem for minimal projective varieties satisfying Miyaoka's equality') is reported by a search summary and was not checked on the v1 page.
events.delivers: For projective klt varieties satisfying Miyaoka's equality 3c_2 = c_1^2 with K_X nef in the minimal setting: K_X semiample, kappa in {0,1,2}, and an explicit Iitaka fibration structure. The restriction is the Miyaoka equality class; the statement is for varieties, not pairs. The paper also states a similar result for projective klt varieties with nef anti-canonical divisor.
events.remains: Abundance for minimal projective klt varieties not satisfying Miyaoka's equality, in every dimension; that is, the general case of the bullet is untouched.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper; the arXiv v4 comment reads 'To appear in Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society'. A search also surfaced a Proc. LMS 131(6) e70104 record in Osaka University's repository, which I did not open.

events.doubts: No reader objection, correction or failed-step report was found. The version history shows substantial change: v3 changed the title and altered the main result, and v4 removed Section 5 and revised two further sections. The scope of the printed theorem should be compared with the v1 claim before relying on it; I did not do that comparison.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: it proves the semiampleness conclusion in the Miyaoka-equality subclass and does not contradict it.

events.what_happened: Vladimir Lazic posts arXiv:2406.18233, 'Metrics with minimal singularities and the Abundance conjecture' (26 Jun 2024, one version). For a minimal projective klt pair (X, Delta) with chi(X, O_X) nonzero, the paper gives a necessary and sufficient condition for K_X + Delta to be semiample, phrased as an approximation property of multiplier ideals of currents with minimal singularities. It also proves structural results on supercanonical currents, which the author says are 'central to the completion of the proof'. Theorem A is conditional on existence of good minimal models for projective klt pairs in dimensions at most n - 1.
events.revisions: v1 only (26 Jun 2024).
events.delivers: An equivalence: under chi nonzero and the lower-dimensional MMP, abundance for minimal klt pairs holds if and only if an approximation property of minimal-singularity currents holds; with the MMP in lower dimensions, if kappa >= 0 or chi nonzero then K + Delta is semiample given that property. It covers pairs (Delta allowed) and does not settle any case unconditionally in the paper's own framing.
events.remains: The approximation property (which the paper does not prove); the chi = 0 case, where the paper says very little is known in higher dimensions unless X is uniruled; the general conjecture in every dimension.
events.time_since_posted: about 2 years 3 months (to 10 Oct 2026); no commentary found in my searches, and citing papers were not systematically checked
events.doubts: The result is conditional on the MMP in lower dimensions and on the approximation property, which the author has not established; the abstract says the results 'indicate strongly' the direction of the proof rather than completing it. No reader's critique was found.
events.direction: Reduction: it identifies a necessary and sufficient condition for the conclusion of the conjecture when chi is nonzero. It neither supports nor contradicts the conjecture unconditionally.

events.what_happened: Jihao Liu and Zheng Xu post arXiv:2505.05250, 'Non-vanishing implies numerical dimension one abundance' (v1 8 May 2025, v2 30 Jul 2025). Main results: (i) unconditionally, smooth projective varieties of dimension at most 5 with kappa >= 0 and nu <= 1 have a good minimal model, so kappa = nu (Thm 1.2); (ii) unconditionally, smooth projective varieties of dimension at most 4 with chi(O_X) nonzero and nu <= 1 (Cor 1.3); (iii) conditionally on the non-vanishing conjecture in dimension d, smooth projective varieties of dimension at most d with nu <= 1 (Thm 1.4); (iv) the lc versions (Thm 5.1, 5.4); (v) for projective klt pairs with 0 <= kappa_sigma <= 1 under the chi condition (Cor 5.2); (vi) a relative klt statement (Thm 6.6) under one of three hypotheses, including d - kappa <= 5.
events.revisions: v1 8 May 2025; v2 30 Jul 2025 (no change note found in the abstract page).
events.delivers: Unconditionally for smooth projective varieties: kappa = nu in dimension at most 5 when kappa >= 0 and nu <= 1, and in dimension at most 4 when chi nonzero and nu <= 1. For klt pairs the unconditional statement (Cor 5.2) is under the chi condition and dimension at most 4, as read from the paper's corollary-by-corollary summary. Conditionally on non-vanishing (Thm 1.4) or special termination (Thm 1.6), the nu <= 1 case holds in arbitrary dimension d for smooth varieties. The paper's general statements concern nu <= 1 only.
events.remains: All of the bullet for nu >= 2 (any dimension >= 2); kappa < 0 cases, which need non-vanishing; smooth varieties of dimension at least 5 without the conditional hypotheses; klt varieties with chi = 0 in dimension at least 2 for nu <= 1 unless covered by Thm 6.6's hypotheses.
events.time_since_posted: about 17 months (to 10 Oct 2026); no commentary found in my searches
events.doubts: The unconditional results are restricted to nu <= 1 and, for klt, to chi nonzero and dimension at most 4; the abstract's phrase 'dimension at most 5, unconditionally' applies to smooth varieties. The abstract does not state the restriction for klt pairs; I read it from Cor 5.2 and Cor 1.3 in the full text, which I did not finish (the page was truncated at about 117k characters, and the last 17k were not read).
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: confirms kappa = nu, which is the content of abundance, in the listed special cases; it does not contradict the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Osamu Fujino posts arXiv:2506.00760, 'On finiteness of relative log pluricanonical representations' (v1 1 Jun 2025). In the complex analytic setting it reduces the abundance conjecture for semi-log canonical pairs to the log canonical case, and reduces abundance for projective morphisms of complex analytic spaces to the classical projective abundance conjecture. The paper states the projective abundance for lc pairs (its Conjecture 1.9) has been solved in dimension at most 3 and 'when dim X >= 4, it is still widely open'.
events.revisions: v1 1 Jun 2025; v2 29 Jul 2026 (major revision after the referee's report).
events.delivers: Reductions only: analytic abundance for slc to lc, and analytic relative abundance to the projective case (its Theorem 1.10 and Cor 1.11 assume projective lc abundance in dimension n). Nothing in the projective klt case is established in the paper.
events.remains: The projective klt (or lc) abundance in dimension at least 4, which the paper itself treats as the input it does not supply.
events.time_since_posted: about 16 months (v1 to 10 Oct 2026); no commentary found in my searches
events.doubts: The v2 'major revisions following the referee's report' indicates refereeing of some kind; the report's content is not public as far as I found. The results are reductions and are not reasons to doubt anything in the projective case.
events.direction: Reduction in the analytic setting; cuts toward the conjecture or is neutral. It does not touch the projective klt statement.

events.what_happened: Swapnajit Das posts arXiv:2604.28085, 'Abundance for semi log canonical compact Kahler threefolds' (v1 30 Apr 2026, v2 13 Sep 2026, major revision). Theorem 1.3: for a compact Kahler slc threefold pair with nef K + Delta, the divisor is semiample. Cor 1.4: on the Fujiki class C subclass, a nef but not numerically trivial slc pair is semiample. Theorem 1.5: an irreducible slc threefold in Fujiki class C with nef canonical divisor that is not semiample (H^0(X, mK_X) = 0 for large divisible m). The v2 comment says the counterexample claimed in v1 is not valid in the compact Kahler setting (Zhiyuan Jiang pointed out that its variety is not Kahler although its normalization is), and that it remains valid only in Fujiki class C; the v2 comment also says abundance is now proved in full generality for compact Kahler slc pairs. The acknowledgements thank Janos Kollar for identifying an error in a previous arXiv version.
events.revisions: v1 30 Apr 2026 (contained a counterexample in the compact Kahler setting, later withdrawn in that setting); v2 13 Sep 2026 (major revision; counterexample kept only in Fujiki class C; Kahler abundance proved).
events.delivers: For compact Kahler slc threefolds (not projective, not klt): abundance (nef implies semiample) in dimension 3, with the Fujiki class C subcase; and a non-semiample nef slc threefold in Fujiki class C. Neither is a projective klt result.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet, since the paper concerns the Kahler slc class; projective klt varieties are not addressed.

checked_by.qualification: Senior algebraic geometer working in birational geometry
checked_by.what_they_did: Identified an error in a previous arXiv version (per the v2 acknowledgements; the error concerned the earlier counterexample's status).

checked_by.qualification: Researcher in Kahler birational geometry (see Jiang 2026 entry)
checked_by.what_they_did: Pointed out that the earlier counterexample's variety is not Kahler (per the v2 comment and acknowledgements).

events.doubts: The earlier version's counterexample was withdrawn in the Kahler setting after a specific error was identified by Jiang, and the acknowledgements credit Kollar with identifying an error in an earlier version, which the v2 text says conflicted with other claims (an etale double cover). The Fujiki class C counterexample remains. Whether the v2 proof of Kahler abundance is correct was not checked.

withdrawn.what: The v1 counterexample to slc abundance was declared invalid in the compact Kahler setting; v2 keeps it only for Fujiki class C.

events.direction: Mixed, but outside the bullet's class: proves semiampleness for Kahler slc threefolds (consistent with the conjecture's form) and exhibits a non-semiample nef slc threefold in Fujiki class C, which is neither projective nor klt.
events.object: An irreducible slc threefold in Fujiki class C (not projective, not klt) with nef canonical divisor, not semiample: H^0(X, mK_X) = 0 for all sufficiently large and divisible m. Whether the construction is explicit or an existence argument was not checked from the text I read.

events.what_happened: Zhiyuan Jiang posts arXiv:2604.03879, 'An approach to the abundance conjecture for Kahler varieties via algebraic reduction' (4 Apr 2026, v1 only). The paper formulates the conjecture for Kahler lc pairs (K_X + Delta nef implies semiample), notes it was originally stated for projective varieties, and states 'The abundance conjecture is open in dimension >= 4.' Theorem 1.1 is an inductive reduction using the algebraic reduction fibration, assuming projective MMP and abundance in dimension a(X), Kahler abundance in lower dimension, and related inputs. Theorem 1.2: a compact Kahler fourfold X with algebraic dimension 3 and nef K_X has K_X semiample. Theorem 1.3 (per a search summary; not checked in the text): klt threefolds with a(X) nonzero.
events.revisions: v1 only (4 Apr 2026).
events.delivers: For compact Kahler (generally non-projective) varieties: a reduction of the Kahler case to the projective case under stated inputs, and, in dimension 4, abundance for non-algebraic Kahler fourfolds with a(X) = 3 and nef K_X. These are analogues in the Kahler class, not the projective klt statement.
events.remains: The projective klt case in all dimensions (the bullet), and the Kahler case in dimension at least 4 apart from the listed cases.
events.time_since_posted: about 6 months (to 10 Oct 2026); no commentary found in my searches
events.doubts: The paper rests on several projective inputs (MMP and abundance in dimension a(X), the moduli b-divisor result of Ambro, and others) and on a b-good nef moduli b-divisor hypothesis; whether those hypotheses are satisfied in the cases claimed was not checked. The single-author, single-version preprint has no public review found.
events.direction: Analogue: partial confirmation in the Kahler class; does not contradict the conjecture. The paper itself says the conjecture is open in dimension at least 4.

events.what_happened: Makoto Enokizono and Nao Moriyama post arXiv:2609.12478, 'Abundance theorem for log surfaces' (v1 11 Sep 2026, v2 5 Oct 2026). Theorem 1.1: for a log surface (X, Delta) (normal surface over an algebraically closed field, boundary R-divisor, K_X + Delta R-Cartier, with no Q-factoriality or log canonicity assumed) and a proper surjective morphism pi: X -> S, if K_X + Delta is pi-nef then it is pi-semiample. The paper says it generalises the earlier abundance theorems for Q-factorial and lc log surfaces (Fujita 1984; Fong-McKernan 1992; Fujino 2012; Tanaka 2014).
events.revisions: v1 11 Sep 2026; v2 5 Oct 2026 (the version the page shows; changes not identified).
events.delivers: Dimension 2 only: abundance for log surfaces, with pairs and relative morphisms, under no Q-factorial or lc hypothesis. The problem's klt surfaces are a subcase; klt surfaces are Q-factorial (a standard fact, not stated as such in the paper), so they were already covered by the earlier Q-factorial surface results the paper cites. The new content is the removal of Q-factoriality and lc for surfaces, which the bullet does not need.
events.remains: Dimension 3 and higher, which is most of the bullet. The paper itself says nothing about threefolds or higher dimensions.
events.doubts: No engagement yet. The claim is a surface theorem, and surface abundance for klt pairs was known before, so the scope relative to the bullet is narrow. The paper's text was read to about 100k of 108k characters.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: proves the conclusion for log surfaces in a larger class than the bullet's surface case. It does not move the question in dimension at least 3.

events.what_happened: Andreas Hoering, Vladimir Lazic and Christian Lehn post arXiv:2508.14634, 'Nonvanishing results for Kahler varieties' (v1 20 Aug 2025, v2 21 Oct 2025). Theorem A: for a Q-factorial compact Kahler klt pair (X, Delta) with X not uniruled, K_X + Delta nef of numerical dimension 1 and chi(X, O_X) nonzero, kappa(X, K_X + Delta) >= 0. The paper notes that when X is projective and good minimal models exist in lower dimensions, this gives semiampleness of K_X + Delta.
events.revisions: v1 20 Aug 2025; v2 21 Oct 2025 (minor corrections, added details).
events.delivers: Non-vanishing (kappa >= 0) for Kahler klt pairs with nu = 1 and chi nonzero, non-uniruled; it is an ingredient of abundance, and a conditional semiampleness consequence in the projective case. It is not an abundance theorem in its own right.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet outside nu = 1 with chi nonzero, non-uniruled, Kahler; also the uniruled and chi = 0 cases.
events.time_since_posted: about 14 months (v1 to 10 Oct 2026); no commentary found in my searches
events.doubts: Non-vanishing is a different statement from abundance. The projective consequence is conditional on lower-dimensional good minimal models. The v2 change note concerns minor inaccuracies.
events.direction: Partial ingredient for the conjecture in a Kahler class; neutral on the projective klt statement unless the lower-dimensional inputs are supplied.

events.what_happened: Mu-Lin Li, Sheng Rao and Kai Wang post arXiv:2510.23967, 'Deformation of nef adjoint canonical line bundles' (v1 28 Oct 2025, only version). It proves deformation results for nef and semiample adjoint canonical bundles in smooth families (Thm 1.1, 1.5, 1.8, 1.10), and an abundance statement for normal Q-factorial compact Kahler terminal threefolds (Thm 1.11). Remark 4.5 records that a result of Fujino is conditional on abundance for a projective klt pair.
events.revisions: v1 only (28 Oct 2025).
events.delivers: Deformation statements for nef adjoint canonical bundles in smooth families; a Kahler terminal threefold abundance statement. It does not prove abundance for projective klt varieties and is discounted for the bullet.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.time_since_posted: about 12 months (to 10 Oct 2026); no commentary found
events.doubts: None raised. Recorded as a neighbouring result on nef adjoint canonical bundles, not as a claim on the bullet.
events.direction: Neutral for the bullet.

events.what_happened: Yujiro Kawamata, 'Abundance theorem for minimal threefolds', Invent. Math. 108 (1992), 229-246. Cited as such in Kawamata's KAKEN grant report (1992 annual report; project 'Number theory of algebraic varieties', 1991-1992). The paper itself was not opened. Its content as the abundance theorem in dimension 3 is taken from secondary statements (Demailly-Peternell 2003 as cited in the search summary; Fujino 2025, which says the projective lc abundance conjecture is solved in dimension at most 3, and the Wikipedia-based claim that dimension 3 is settled).
events.delivers: Abundance for minimal threefolds (dimension 3), per the secondary statements; for the bullet this is the dimension-3 case of klt or lc varieties, subject to the paper's exact hypotheses, which were not read.
events.remains: Dimension 4 and higher, which is the open part according to Fujino 2025 and Jiang 2026.
events.doubts: The exact hypotheses (terminal, canonical, klt, lc, characteristic) were not checked from the paper. This entry rests on the KAKEN citation and on secondary statements.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture in dimension 3 (for the hypotheses the paper uses).

events.what_happened: Yum-Tong Siu posts arXiv:0912.0576, 'Abundance conjecture' (v1 3 Dec 2009, v2 13 Jan 2010, v3 26 Jun 2010), which 'sketches a proof' of the abundance conjecture in the form kappa(X) = kappa_num(X) for a compact complex algebraic manifold. The sketch has three parts: the case of numerical Kodaira dimension zero (described in detail), the general case under a foliation-fibration coincidence assumption, and a sketch of verifying that coincidence. The paper says complete details will appear elsewhere; I did not find a write-up.
events.delivers: A claimed sketch for smooth complex algebraic (hence projective) manifolds, which are klt; if complete, it would cover the smooth case of the bullet in the Kodaira-dimension form. It is a sketch, not a proof, and says nothing about singular klt varieties.
events.remains: A complete proof, including the coincidence step and the general case; klt singular varieties.

checked_by.qualification: Algebraic geometer working on numerical Kodaira dimension and the abundance conjecture (author of arXiv:1505.01262)
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave the talk 'On Siu's Approach to Abundance Conjecture' on 16 Jan 2013, presenting Siu's strategy and stating that the construction of a 'good' numerically trivial foliation on a projective non-uniruled complex manifold still needs further investigation. This is an identified unresolved step, not a verification.

events.doubts: The abstract calls the work a sketch. The 2013 talk abstract names an unresolved step (the good numerically trivial foliation) in Siu's strategy, and I found no later verification or closure of that step. The claimed proof is therefore not accepted by the field as far as I found, and no retraction was found.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture (in the smooth case) for all compact complex algebraic manifolds; the claim is unverified.

events.what_happened: Yujiro Kawamata posts 'A remark on the abundance conjecture' (arXiv:1101.0214, v1 31 Dec 2010), and withdraws it on 4 Jan 2011 ('due to a crucial error'). The withdrawn abstract gives no content. A search summary describes its intended content as abundance in dimension n following from existence of minimal models in dimension n, abundance in lower dimensions and non-vanishing in dimension n; I could not confirm that from the page, which carries only the withdrawal notice.
events.revisions: v1 31 Dec 2010; v2 4 Jan 2011 (withdrawn).
events.delivers: Nothing established: the claimed reduction was withdrawn for a crucial error. Recorded so that the withdrawal is visible.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet, on this record.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the author for a crucial error.

withdrawn.what: The reduction of abundance in dimension n to minimal models, lower-dimensional abundance and non-vanishing, as described in the search summary.

events.direction: Unknown; the content of the withdrawn version is not visible.

events.what_happened: Thomas Eckl posts arXiv:1505.01262, 'Numerical analogues of the Kodaira dimension and the Abundance Conjecture' (v1 6 May 2015, v2 31 Dec 2015, v3 1 Jan 2016); published in Manuscripta Math. 150 (2016), 337-356. It adds notions to Lehmann's list of numerical analogues of the Kodaira dimension, closes a gap in the proof of kappa_nu(D) <= nu_alg(D) (a gap in earlier work by Lehmann), and proves that the Abundance Conjecture of the MMP and the Generalized Abundance Conjecture with these numerical analogues are equivalent for non-uniruled complex projective varieties.
events.delivers: An equivalence between two forms of abundance for non-uniruled projective varieties; it reduces but does not prove abundance.
events.remains: Abundance itself in the non-uniruled projective case, and the uniruled case.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (vol. 150, 2016), per the abstract page and a catalogue reference found in search.

events.doubts: Eckl's equivalence depends on the numerical analogues; its relation to Siu's sketch was not established by the abstract.
events.direction: Reduction; neutral on the conjecture's truth.

events.what_happened: Tobias Dorsch and Vladimir Lazic post arXiv:1406.6554, 'A note on the abundance conjecture' (v1 25 Jun 2014); published in Algebraic Geometry 2 (2015), 476-488. The paper proves that abundance for non-uniruled klt pairs in dimension n implies abundance for uniruled klt pairs in dimension n, assuming the MMP in lower dimensions.
events.revisions: v1 25 Jun 2014 (later versions not checked).
events.delivers: A reduction for klt pairs: the uniruled case follows from the non-uniruled case in the same dimension.
events.remains: The non-uniruled klt case in every dimension.
events.direction: Reduction; neutral on truth.

events.what_happened: Vladimir Lazic and Thomas Peternell post arXiv:1601.01602, 'Abundance for varieties with many differential forms' (v1 7 Jan 2016, v3 12 Feb 2018); published in Epijournal Geom. Algebrique 2 (2018), epiga:3867. Abundance is proved for varieties with mild singularities having many reflexive differential forms with coefficients in pluricanonical bundles, assuming the MMP in lower dimensions; results for numerical dimension 1 are unconditional. Klt pairs appear as a consequence for uniruled varieties.
events.revisions: v1 7 Jan 2016; v2 (not checked); v3 12 Feb 2018.
events.delivers: Abundance under a 'many reflexive forms' hypothesis, mostly conditional on the MMP in lower dimensions; unconditional for numerical dimension 1. The inclusion of klt varieties in the main theorem was not read from the abstract page.
events.remains: Varieties without many reflexive forms, which is most of the bullet.

checked_by.who: Epijournal de Geometrie Algebrique (journal of record)

events.direction: Partial confirmation in a special class; does not contradict the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Omprokash Das and Joe Waldron post arXiv:1610.03403, 'On the Abundance Problem for 3-folds in characteristic p > 5' (v1 11 Oct 2016, v2 3 May 2017, v3 30 Aug 2018, with an appendix by Christopher Hacon); published in Math. Z. (DOI 10.1007/s00209-018-2110-5). Two cases: (i) (X, Delta) klt with kappa(X, K_X + Delta) = 1 (semiample); (ii) (X, 0) klt with K_X numerically trivial and X not uniruled.
events.revisions: v1 11 Oct 2016; v2 3 May 2017; v3 30 Aug 2018 (references and minor changes).
events.delivers: Dimension 3, klt, characteristic p > 5: abundance when kappa = 1, and when K_X is numerically trivial and X is non-uniruled. Not characteristic zero; restricted to dimension 3.
events.remains: Characteristic p <= 5; dimension 4 and higher; the other kappa values in dimension 3 for klt pairs.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture in dimension 3 for characteristic p > 5 in the two stated cases.

events.what_happened: Caucher Birkar posts arXiv:1104.4981, 'Existence of log canonical flips and a special LMMP' (v1 26 Apr 2011; v3 24 Apr 2012); published in Publ. Math. IHES 115 (2012). For a Q-factorial dlt pair (X/Z, B + A) with K_X + B + A numerically trivial over Z, an LMMP/Z on K_X + B with scaling terminates with a good log minimal model or a Mori fibre space; a corollary gives log flip existence for lc pairs. The paper never uses the word 'abundance'.
events.delivers: Termination of a special LMMP with good minimal model conclusion for Q-factorial dlt pairs in the relative numerically-trivial setting; not an abundance theorem for klt varieties in the bullet's sense.
events.remains: All of the bullet on this paper's terms.
events.doubts: The Wikipedia article's only status sentence, 'Important cases of the abundance conjecture have been proven by Caucher Birkar', cites this paper. The paper does not contain an abundance theorem of that type on the abstract page, so the citation does not show which cases are meant; I could not identify them.
events.direction: Neutral; a termination statement that is a neighbour to abundance.

events.what_happened: Priyankur Chaudhuri posts arXiv:2108.02332, 'Nef and abundant divisors, semiampleness and canonical bundle formula' (v1 5 Aug 2021, v2 3 Sep 2022); published in Int. J. Math. (2022). For a klt pair (X, B) with K_X + B effective and a nef line bundle L, if K_X + B + L is nef and abundant then it is semiample; this generalises a theorem of Kawamata to the generalised-abundance setting.
events.delivers: A conditional semiampleness statement for klt pairs with a nef line bundle added; the 'nef and abundant' hypothesis is the abundance-type input. Not a proof of the bullet.
events.remains: The bullet, since nefness plus abundance is assumed.

checked_by.who: International Journal of Mathematics (journal of record)

events.direction: Neutral; a conditional neighbour.

events.what_happened: Fabio Bernasconi, Iacopo Brivio and Liam Stigant post arXiv:2111.08970, 'Abundance theorem for threefolds in mixed characteristic' (v1 17 Nov 2021, v2 23 Nov 2022; accepted in Math. Ann.). They prove the abundance theorem for arithmetic klt threefold pairs whose closed points have residue characteristic greater than 5, and a plurigenera invariance consequence for surface pairs.
events.revisions: v1 17 Nov 2021; v2 23 Nov 2022 (accepted in Math. Ann., per the comment field).
events.delivers: Dimension 3, klt, arithmetic (mixed characteristic) with residue characteristic above 5. A restricted case of the bullet in a setting outside characteristic zero.
events.remains: Dimension 4 and higher; residue characteristic 5 and below.
events.doubts: Acceptance is stated in the comment field only; the journal volume was not found. The Brivio talk of 13 Sep 2024 (CMSA) described a sketch for mixed characteristic threefolds based on this joint work; I did not open the talk page, and it is not treated as a separate event.
events.direction: Partial confirmation in dimension 3 (mixed characteristic, residue characteristic above 5); does not contradict the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Zheng Xu posts arXiv:2212.04039, 'Note on the 3-dimensional log canonical abundance in characteristic > 3' (v1 8 Dec 2022, v2 3 Feb 2024 with corrections; 'to appear in Nagoya Math. J.'). Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 3, for projective lc threefold pairs (X, B): non-vanishing (kappa(K_X + B) >= 0 when pseudo-effective); abundance when K_X + B is nef and kappa >= 1 (semiample); abundance for klt threefold pairs implies abundance for lc threefold pairs; and applications. Nagoya Math. J. records online publication on 28 Feb 2024; that date is not used for this event.
events.revisions: v1 8 Dec 2022; v2 3 Feb 2024 ('made some corrections and fixed some typos'); Nagoya Math. J. online 28 Feb 2024 (from the Cambridge listing in search results).
events.delivers: Dimension 3, lc (hence klt) projective pairs, characteristic p > 3: abundance when kappa >= 1 (and nef). Restricted to kappa >= 1 and to characteristic above 3.
events.remains: kappa = 0 and kappa = -infinity cases; characteristic 2 and 3; dimension 4 and higher.
events.direction: Partial confirmation in dimension 3 under kappa >= 1 and characteristic above 3.

events.what_happened: Zheng Xu posts arXiv:2307.03938, 'Abundance for threefolds in positive characteristic when nu = 2' (v1 8 Jul 2023, v2 27 Aug 2025, v3 17 Apr 2026, 'final version, to appear in Compositio Mathematica'). For a projective lc threefold pair (X, B) over a perfect field of characteristic p > 3, K_X + B nef with numerical dimension 2 implies semiample.
events.revisions: v1 8 Jul 2023 (algebraically closed field); v2 27 Aug 2025 (extended to perfect field, typos); v3 17 Apr 2026 ('to appear in Compositio Mathematica').

events.remains: nu in {0, 1, 3} and the other pieces; dimension at least 4; characteristic 2 and 3.

events.what_happened: Omprokash Das and Wenhao Ou post arXiv:2201.01202, 'On the Log Abundance for Compact Kahler 3-folds' (v1 4 Jan 2022, v3 21 Feb 2023, accepted in Manuscripta Math.). For a log canonical compact Kahler threefold pair with K_X + Delta nef and numerical dimension not 2, K_X + Delta is semiample.
events.delivers: Kahler threefolds, lc pairs, numerical dimension not 2. Analogue, not projective; partial in dimension 3.
events.remains: Numerical dimension 2 in the Kahler class; projective varieties are not the setting here.

events.what_happened: Osamu Fujino posts arXiv:0803.1691, 'Finite generation of the log canonical ring in dimension four' (v1 12 Mar 2008, v2 23 Apr 2009, v3 23 Sep 2009); published in Kyoto J. Math. 50 (2010), 671-684. Includes the abundance theorem for irregular fourfolds (q nonzero), proved by traditional arguments, derived from the MMP and abundance in dimension at most 3; the general statement is for irregular (n+1)-folds assuming MMP and abundance in dimension at most n. Section 5 was removed in v3 for a conceptual mistake (concerning log plurigenera in dimension 3).
events.revisions: v1 12 Mar 2008; v2 23 Apr 2009; v3 23 Sep 2009 (Section 5 removed).
events.delivers: Dimension 4, irregular case (q nonzero): abundance under the stated inputs. A restricted class of fourfolds; the search summary adds canonical singularities, which I did not confirm from the abstract.
events.remains: Regular fourfolds (q = 0) in dimension 4, which the paper does not treat.

events.what_happened: Kenta Hashizume, 'Remarks on the abundance conjecture', Proc. Japan Acad. Ser. A 92(9) (2016), 101-106. The paper proves the abundance theorem for log canonical n-folds with big boundary, assuming abundance for lc (n-1)-folds, and discusses the log MMP for lc 4-folds. The preprint date was not checked; a search result with the same title carries arXiv:1509.04626, which I did not open.
events.delivers: Log canonical pairs with big boundary, with abundance in dimension n-1 as input. A partial result for lc pairs.
events.remains: The non-big boundary case; the conjecture in dimension n without the lower-dimensional input.

events.what_happened: Kenta Hashizume, 'Minimal model program for normal pairs along log canonical locus', arXiv:2310.13904 (v1 21 Oct 2023); published in Forum Math. Sigma 13 (2025), e143. For a normal pair (X, Delta) with projective X -> Z and relatively ample A: under two hypotheses (the non-nef locus of K_X + Delta + A over Z misses the non-lc locus of (X, Delta), and the restriction to the non-lc locus is semiample over Z), termination of an MMP on (X, Delta + A)/Z and abundance for its minimal model.
events.revisions: v1 21 Oct 2023 (later versions not checked).
events.delivers: Conditional abundance for the minimal model of a normal lc-type pair under the two stated hypotheses. Pairs, relative, lc locus; not klt varieties in general.
events.remains: The bullet, in the form without the two hypotheses.

disputes.summary: Siu's 2009 sketch of the smooth (Kodaira dimension) case: the 2013 Eckl talk names the good numerically trivial foliation as the unresolved step; no closure was found in my searches. Not a priority dispute; recorded as an open gap.

Das (2026) slc Kahler counterexample: v1 counterexample invalid in the Kahler setting (pointed out by Jiang; Kollar identified an error in an earlier arXiv version); v2 keeps a counterexample only in Fujiki class C. Not projective and not klt, so it does not bear on the bullet directly.
Kawamata's 2010 remark on the abundance conjecture was withdrawn on 4 Jan 2011 for a crucial error.

The Wikipedia article's status sentence ('Important cases of the abundance conjecture have been proven by Caucher Birkar') cites Birkar 1104.4981, whose abstract contains a termination and good-model statement for Q-factorial dlt pairs and no abundance theorem; the cases meant are not identified.

summary: Searches (43 calls, listed below) and reads of the primary sources found no proof of the abundance conjecture for projective klt varieties posted since 26 January 2024, and no AI involvement in the mathematics of any abundance result in the window. The in-window events are: Iwai-Matsumura-Muller (April 2024), which proves semiampleness of K_X for klt varieties with Miyaoka's equality; Lazic (June 2024), a conditional equivalence for minimal klt pairs with chi nonzero; Liu-Xu (May 2025), unconditional for smooth projective varieties of dimension at most 5 with kappa >= 0 and nu <= 1 and for klt pairs of dimension at most 4 with chi nonzero, with the rest conditional on non-vanishing or special termination; Fujino (June 2025), reductions in the analytic setting; Hoering-Lazic-Lehn (August 2025), non-vanishing for Kahler klt pairs; Li-Rao-Wang (October 2025), a deformation result that does not bear on the bullet; Das (April 2026, revised September 2026), Kahler and Fujiki-class slc results with a withdrawn-in-part counterexample; Jiang (April 2026), a Kahler reduction and fourfold cases, stating that the conjecture is open in dimension at least 4; and Enokizono-Moriyama (September 2026), abundance for log surfaces without Q-factoriality or lc hypotheses. Every in-window projective-klt result is restricted: the strongest unconditional projective cases are smooth varieties of dimension at most 5 with nu <= 1 (Liu-Xu) and the Miyaoka-equality class (Iwai et al.). The pre-window history is extensive and I have recorded it as events: Kawamata's threefold theorem (1992, from the KAKEN citation and secondary statements), Siu's claimed smooth-case sketch (2009, with a flagged unresolved step), a withdrawn Kawamata remark (2011), several reductions and partial results (Dorsch-Lazic 2014, Eckl 2015, Lazic-Peternell 2016, Das-Waldron 2016, Chaudhuri 2021, Bernasconi-Brivio-Stigant 2021, Das-Ou 2022, Xu 2022 and 2023, Hashizume 2016 and 2023, Fujino 2008) and Birkar 2011. Close calls: (1) whether Iwai et al. or Liu-Xu's special cases count as a restricted resolution of the bullet, or only as a moved bound, depends on how the judging pass weighs classes of varieties against the full statement; (2) Enokizono-Moriyama proves a theorem in dimension 2 that is already covered for klt surfaces by older results (klt surfaces are Q-factorial, a standard fact I have not seen stated in the paper), so it adds no new klt case; (3) Das's Kahler slc counterexample is outside the projective klt class, though it shows the conjecture fails in some non-projective settings with slc singularities. The AI search covered: abundance with AI and model terms; AI claims about algebraic geometry and minimal model programs; lab announcements (OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic); the Epoch AI FrontierMath open problems list (10 of 49 items visible, none in this area); the DeepMind formal-conjectures repository (top-level folders only); and Tao's blog (nothing relevant). The adjacent AI events in the window are not about abundance: OpenAI's May 2026 disproof of Erdos's unit distance conjecture (discrete geometry); DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus (arXiv:2605.22763, May 2026), whose algebraic geometry result is reported as Zanello's log-concavity conjecture for O-sequences, with no abundance mention in the abstract; and a reported Jacobian conjecture counterexample credited to Anthropic's Claude, which I did not verify and which concerns a different problem. Dates use first public written argument (arXiv v1 or the first journal-free posting); journal publication dates are recorded only in the entries' revisions and checked_by fields. The Wikipedia article states the conjecture for every projective variety with klt singularities over a field k and was last edited 24 Aug 2026; I did not check the January 2024 revision.
competing_reading: A stronger reading would count Iwai-Matsumura-Muller (Miyaoka-equality klt varieties with semiample canonical bundle), Liu-Xu's unconditional smooth dimension-5 result, and Enokizono-Moriyama's surface theorem as genuine progress on the bullet, because each proves the stated conclusion for a class of projective klt varieties and the bullet is a universal statement over a class that includes these. The weaker reading, which I think the text supports, is that each is a restricted case (a special class of varieties, a special range of kappa and nu, or a dimension at most 4 or 5 that the bullet does not restrict), so the bullet is unsettled in the general case and in dimension at least 4, as Jiang (2026) and Fujino (2025) both state. A third reading treats the Kahler and slc results as counting toward the bullet because the paper of Jiang and the paper of Das work with compact Kahler varieties that include projective ones; but the bullet is about projective varieties, and the Kahler statements do not decide the projective statement either way.
what_would_settle_it: A complete proof of abundance for projective klt varieties in every dimension would settle the bullet; a counterexample to it in the projective klt class would refute it. Short of that, the closest checkable evidence is (a) the full text of Iwai-Matsumura-Muller's final theorem and the journal version, to see whether the Miyaoka-equality class is what the journal printed; (b) the Liu-Xu klt corollaries (Cor 5.2 and Thm 6.6) read in full to confirm the chi and dimension restrictions for klt varieties; (c) a check of whether Enokizono-Moriyama's surface theorem covers klt surfaces without the Q-factorial reduction; (d) the Kawamata 1992 paper's exact hypotheses; and (e) the identity of the 'important cases' Wikipedia attributes to Birkar, which would show whether any klt case beyond dimension 3 is known.
